entitySuffixRule: Must contain the words "limited liability company," the abbreviation "L.L.C." or "LLC," or words or abbreviations of like import in another language written in roman characters. The name may not contain the word "corporation" or "incorporated," or an abbreviation of either.
distinguishabilityNote: Must be distinguishable upon the records of the Secretary of State from the name of, or for, every other entity, whether that name is true, assumed, reserved, or registered. Tennessee screens against assumed names too, not just live entity names. Section 48-249-106(c) gives three routes past a conflict: the prior holder consents in writing AND undertakes to cancel or change its own name (Written Consent for Use of Indistinguishable Name, SS-9411, $20); the applicant delivers a certified copy of a final court judgment establishing its right to the name; or the prior holder consents in writing and both parties agree to use the same registered agent. Consent on its own is not one of the three.
nameReservationCostBasis: The $20 Secretary of State fee (Application for Name Reservation, SS-9425) is the full cost.
notes: Tennessee publishes no free official copy of its code: the General Assembly's own 'Tennessee Code' link (wapp.capitol.tn.gov Links page) hands off to lexisnexis.com/hottopics/tncode, and no state host carries the code text, so the mirror citations below are kept under the README exception with the enacted Public Chapters as the corroborating official source. Per the code's history line, § 48-249-106 was enacted by Acts 2005, ch. 286, § 1 and amended once by Acts 2006, ch. 620, § 16 (deleting the last sentence of former (d)(3)); § 48-249-107 was enacted by Acts 2005, ch. 286, § 1 and never amended. Both chapters were read in full from the Legislature's own PDF archive and match the mirrors' 2024 code text. Tennessee does not publish a fixed list of banned words; instead § 48-249-106(a)(2) bars any language stating or implying that the LLC may transact a business needing state authorization (banking, insurance, trust powers, and the like) unless the appropriate commission or official certifies the authorization to the Secretary of State, and it bars implying affiliation with a fraternal, veterans', religious, charitable, or professional organization or with an agency of the United States. A reservation lasts four months with no renewal step; § 48-249-107 says that once it expires the same party or any other party may apply for the same name, and a reservation may be transferred by notice (Notice of Cancellation or Transfer of Reserved Name, SS-4406, $20). On fees, the official schedule prints Articles of Organization (SS-4270) as $300 with an asterisk for per-member variation, and the Secretary of State's business FAQ states the LLC annual report rule verbatim: $300 minimum, increasing by an additional $50 per member for every member over 6, up to a $3,000 maximum.
